references.text: The scarlet cord is first mentioned here as the sign the spies gave to Rahab to mark her house during the conquest of Jericho.
Rahab made an agreement with the spies for protection for herself and her family, which she confirms here with the words 'as you have said, so it shall be'.
The fulfillment of the promise to Rahab - Joshua sent the two spies to bring her and her family out before the city was destroyed.
Rahab was spared because she hid the spies that Joshua had sent, and she lived among the Israelites.
The blood on the doorposts in Egypt served as a sign of salvation, just as the scarlet cord in Rahab's window was a sign of salvation.
The book of Hebrews mentions Rahab's faith as an example - she welcomed the spies and therefore was not destroyed with the unbelievers.
James mentions Rahab as an example that faith is shown through deeds - she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way.
